Tessa / Aditya —

Quick legal take and proposed language to send to Stratus. I kept it concise for procurement. High-level reactions first:

- 99.98% is materially more aggressive than our standard 99.95% for this tier and would significantly increase credit exposure. Recommend we hold to 99.95% and offer a limited uplift only under a negotiated enterprise addendum.
- Unlimited/un-capped credits are not acceptable. We should cap monthly credits at a percentage of monthly recurring fees (recommend 20%) and an annual cap (recommend 200% of one month).
- Notice: 72 hours for standard scheduled maintenance is reasonable; propose 48–72 hours depending on classification (routine vs major).
- Downtime definition: measure per-customer region-level availability for the services actually in scope (not global control plane unless that directly affects their instances). We need explicit measurement POIs.
- Emergency maintenance carveout: we accept an emergency exception but require Redwood to provide post-event notification and a root cause analysis within 72 hours.

Proposed redline snippets (paste these into the Order Form):
"Service Availability. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Service Availability of 99.95% measured monthly for the Services in scope. Availability shall be measured per customer deployment region and calculated as: (Total time in month - Total downtime) / Total time in month.

Service Credits. If Availability for a monthly measurement period falls below 99.95%, Customer may be eligible for Service Credits as set forth below. Service Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for unavailability of the Services. Monthly service credit shall not exceed 20% of the monthly fees for the affected Services; annual aggregate credits shall not exceed 200% of one month’s fees. Service Credits shall not be payable for: (a) scheduled maintenance where Customer received prior notice, (b) Customer-caused issues, or (c) emergency maintenance necessary to address security vulnerabilities.

Maintenance and Notice. Scheduled maintenance will be communicated at least 48 hours in advance for routine maintenance and at least 72 hours for major upgrades. Redwood will aim to limit scheduled maintenance to no more than 8 hours per month; however, exceptions may apply for major upgrades where prior notice is provided.

"

I attached a short doc with tracked language: legal_redlines.docx.

Let me know if you want stronger caps or a different SLA number — I deliberately proposed the 99.95%/20% cap combo to limit exposure while giving Stratus an improvement over baseline.

Thanks — operational notes to feed into the reply and legal redlines:

- Typical maintenance cadence: we perform routine platform patching and model serving updates on a weekly cadence. Standard maintenance window is 02:00–05:00 UTC (which maps to evening/night in US Pacific). Typical per-deployment impact is <30 minutes for rolling config changes; full-host reboots can require up to 60 minutes for a small percentage of capacity while we rebalance traffic.
- We can commit to tooling/processes to keep customer-visible downtime below the thresholds required for credits in most releases (feature flags, rolling restarts, KV/prefix caching). However, there are two caveats: (1) emergency security patches and hypervisor/kernel patches may require immediate action and brief reboots; (2) major model architecture migrations can require longer scheduled windows.
- 8 hours/month cap: operationally reasonable for scheduled maintenance if Stratus agrees to exclude major upgrades and migrations. If they want 8 hours hard cap with no carveouts, that could block critical security rollouts.
- Notice: 72h is fine for routine maintenance. For emergency patches we can provide as much notice as possible and a post-event incident report within 24 hours.

Suggested operational text to include in the runbook link: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/maintenance-runbook-v2

Thanks for the clear markup; we discussed internally and pulled together a proposal that we think is a fair compromise between your ask and Redwood's operational and legal constraints. Attached is a redline of our proposed Order Form language (redwood_proposed-orderform_redline.pdf). Summary below:

1) Availability target: Redwood proposes 99.95% monthly Availability (measured per customer deployment region).
2) Service Credits: Credits trigger when monthly Availability falls below 99.95%. Monthly credits capped at 20% of monthly fees for affected services; annual aggregate cap of 200% of one month. 5) Downtime measurement: Availability measured at the region level for customer instances; formula and sample calculations are in the attached redline.
